ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Beatriz has five sisters with ages of 2, 3, 5, 8, 10 and 17. Beatriz writes these ages in the circles of the opposite diagram, so that the sum of the ages in the four corners of the square is equal to the sum of the ages in the four circles aligned horizontally. What is this sum?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are six empty circles. Four circles are located at the four corners of a diamond-shaped square: top, left, right, bottom; there is also one circle at the center of the diamond; to the right of the right-corner circle there is also an extra circle. On the horizontal line, in order, are the left-corner circle, the center circle, the right-corner circle, and the rightmost extra circle, for a total of four circles. Reasoning: Let the four corners be denoted respectively as T, L, R, B, let the center circle be denoted as C, and let the rightmost extra circle be denoted as O. The problem requires the sum of the four corners to equal the sum of the four horizontal circles, so T+L+R+B = L+C+R+O. Subtract the common L and R from both sides at the same time to get T+B = C+O. Therefore, it is necessary to find two pairs of non-overlapping numbers with equal sums from 2, 3, 5, 8, 10, 17. A feasible one is 3+10 = 13 and 5+8 = 13. Thus T, B, C, O use these four numbers, and the remaining 2 and 17 are placed at L, R. The common sum equals L+R plus the sum of one equal-number pair, namely 2+17+13 = 32.

raw_record.question_text: Beatriz has five sisters with ages 2, 3, 5, 8, 10, and 17. Beatriz writes these ages in the circles of the diagram so that the sum of the ages in the four corners of the square is equal to the sum of the ages in the four circles aligned horizontally. What is this sum?

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as six circles: four corners of the diamond-shaped square (top, left, right, bottom), plus a center circle and an extra circle to the right. The four horizontally aligned circles are left corner, center, right corner, and the extra right circle. From the text, place the six ages 2, 3, 5, 8, 10, 17 so that the corner sum equals the horizontal sum. Label the circles T, L, R, B, C, O. The equality is T+L+R+B = L+C+R+O. Cancel the shared L and R terms to get T+B = C+O. Now find two disjoint pairs among the ages with the same sum; the only possibility is 3+10 = 5+8 = 13. Therefore those four ages occupy T,B,C,O in some order, and the remaining ages 2 and 17 occupy L and R. The common sum is L+R plus one of the equal pair sums: 2+17+13 = 32.

method.method_draft: Read the image as having six total circles. The corner set is the four diamond vertices, while the horizontal set is the left vertex, center, right vertex, and far-right circle. Let the desired common sum be S. The total of all six ages from the text is 2+3+5+8+10+17 = 45. If the two equal sums are added together, every circle is counted once, except the left and right diamond vertices, which are counted twice because they lie both on the square corners and on the horizontal line. Thus 2S = 45 + (sum of the two shared vertex ages). The remaining four non-shared ages must be split into two pairs with equal sums: one pair for top/bottom and one pair for center/far-right. Testing the age list, the only way to split four remaining ages into two equal-sum pairs is to leave 3,5,8,10, since 3+10 = 5+8. Therefore the shared left/right vertex ages must be 2 and 17, with sum 19. Then 2S = 45+19 = 64, so S = 32.
